subject: IronPeak RFI: control mapping, redacted log samples, and upload plan
messages:
From: Aisha Barnes <aisha.barnes@ironpeak.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: procure@ironpeak.com
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI follow-up — control mapping + logs

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. IronPeak is progressing through procurement and our security team has a couple of focused asks that they'd like Redwood to address as part of the RFI (SIG/Q3 questionnaire):

1) Can you provide a control crosswalk (mapping) that ties Redwood controls to SIG v2.0 and ISO 27001 clauses? The security reviewers want explicit mapping fields (control id, description, owner, evidence artifact name).

2) We need redacted telemetry/log samples that show: auth events, KMS key-access records, and a sample application request that includes session-id tracing across the proxy -> runtime path. These should be clearly labeled and have simple instructions for auditors about what each file demonstrates.

3) Clarify hosting options in the context of data residency: hosted API (multi-tenant), dedicated pools, and private VPC installs — what artifacts and attestations differ by mode?

Target: a first artifact bundle by next Thursday; a separate call with your security/infra team would be helpful.

Can you confirm scope and the best secure upload method?

Thanks,
Aisha Barnes
Security Programs
IronPeak Labs

--
Attachment: ironpeak_rfi_scope.pdf (1 page summary)
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Aisha Barnes <aisha.barnes@ironpeak.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, procure@ironpeak.com
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up — control mapping + logs

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear asks. We can deliver the items you listed. High level plan and clarifications below: 

- Control crosswalk: we'll deliver an XLSX that maps Redwood controls to SIG v2.0 identifiers and ISO 27001 clauses, including the artifact filenames and an owner (engineering/product contact).

- Redacted telemetry/logs: we can provide anonymized samples for auth events, KMS access logs (key-use, rotate events), and an example request trace with correlation ids. We will redact PII and redact tenant identifiers but preserve structural fields needed for audit review.

- Hosting options: we'll include an appendix per deployment mode explaining what artifacts change (e.g., private: customer-managed KMS attestations + VPC flow logs; dedicated: reserved GPU pool telemetry; hosted: service-wide telemetry with per-tenant affinity tables).

Questions for you so we scope correctly:
1) Do you need KMS proofs from a specific provider (e.g., AWS KMS with CloudTrail vs. an on-prem HSM export)?
2) For the logs: is CSV ok for the event index and JSON for sample traces?
3) Are there any required retention windows the auditors care about for the samples (we typically provide a 90-day sample slice unless you need a longer lookback)?

We will put together an initial bundle + upload instructions by Thu, 30 Sep 2027. If that works, I'll create a secure, expiring upload folder and send the link (we prefer an encrypted S3 presigned + short-lived token; if you require SFTP or a partner portal we can accommodate).

I'll loop Kimberly (security PM) and Vivek (infra) to confirm owners and artifacts.

—Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: request_acknowledgement.txt
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: IronPeak RFI — artifact plan and redaction notes

Sean — notes from my side after reviewing Aisha's list: 

- Crosswalk: I'll own drafting the spreadsheet. I'll include columns: redwood_control_id, control_description, sig_id, iso_clause, evidence_filename, evidence_type, owner_name, last_review_date.

- Logs: Vivek to produce the KMS/key-access slice and the request-trace exports. We should supply both native CloudTrail lines and a normalized CSV with the fields auditors commonly search on (time, principal, keyId, action, requestId). We'll redact account ids and tenant-id but keep keyId prefixes so auditors can see rotation patterns.

- Encryption attestation: we can include a short key-rotation log (hash + timestamp) and a signed statement from our infra team describing key lifecycle (rotation cadence, who has access). That should satisfy most SIG/ISO reviewers.

- Hosting appendix: I'll write a 1-page matrix that lists which artifacts are available per deployment mode and what additional attestations are possible for Private installs (customer-signed KMS proof, customer-managed logging).

Deliverables I'll prepare for Thu: crosswalk XLSX, redacted log tarball (redwood_sample_logs_redacted.tar.gz), an upload_instructions.txt with steps and presigned link, and a short README for auditors. Vivek—can you confirm you can produce the log slices by EOD Wed?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

--
On Mon, Sep 27, 2027 at 11:05 AM sean_gallagher@redwood.com wrote:
> Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear asks. We can deliver the items you listed...
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Aisha Barnes <aisha.barnes@ironpeak.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, procure@ironpeak.com
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up — control mapping + logs

Aisha — attaching the first artifact bundle per your ask. Summary and next steps below.

Attachments included (in secure upload):
- redwood_sig_crosswalk_v1.xlsx — control map to SIG v2.0 and ISO 27001 (columns: control id, mapping, evidence filename, owner).
- redwood_sample_logs_redacted.tar.gz — 3 redacted files: auth_events_202709_sample.csv, kms_access_202709_sample.json, request_trace_example.json.
- upload_instructions.txt — secure presigned S3 link (expires 72 hours) and MD5 checksums for each file; step-by-step instructions for auditors.
- README-auditor.txt — quick guide to the sample contents and what each file demonstrates.

Quick clarifications:
- KMS proofs: logs are CloudTrail-derived for our AWS KMS keys. If you need HSM exports or a partner-managed KMS proof for a Private deployment, let me know the vendor and we can coordinate (that usually takes 3–5 business days).
- Format: CSV for the event index, JSON for the trace samples. If you request Parquet/NDJSON for bulk ingestion we can provide that as an add-on.
- Retention slice: we've provided a 90-day sample window collapsed to the most relevant events. If your auditors want a longer lookback we can extend to 365 days with legal approval.

Proposed timeline:
- Thu 30 Sep: initial packet delivered (this package).
- Fri 1 Oct: 30-minute technical walk-through with Vivek to go over the logs and the KMS lifecycle evidence (please propose a time).
- Week of Oct 4: follow-up artifacts — e.g., signed attestation on key rotation or private-deploy proof if requested.

Link: secure upload (presigned S3) sent to Aisha via separate email for security.

If this looks good we'll mark the deal progress in HubSpot (IP-2027-09-RFI) and set the technical walkthrough on Friday.

Thanks — Sean
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
